_strings.@@3cf5c9368310: Property Tax Relief Credit (Form RI-1040H, the RI property-tax "circuit breaker") — Must answer YES to ALL eligibility questions on Form RI-1040H Part 1: (A) domiciled in Rhode Island for all of 2025; (B) lived in a household or rented a dwelling that was subject to property tax in 2025; (C) current on property taxes or rent due on the homestead for 2025 and all prior years; (D) you OR your spouse were 65 years of age or older AND/OR disabled as of December 31, 2025; and (E) 2025 total household income was $40,730 or less. Both homeowners (attach the 2025 property tax bill) and renters (attach the 2025 lease or rent receipts; rent paid is multiplied by 20% as deemed property tax) may claim it.

_strings.@@5a1d873d5c71: Treaty conformity — RI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from RI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the RI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: The RI-1040 resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income (2025 RI-1040 Line 1 = federal AGI from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a — the 2025 face prints "line 11a"; instructions Line 3 "Modified Federal Adjusted Gross Income: Determine your modified federal adjusted gross income by combining the amount on line 1 with the amount on line 2"), and the General Instructions state that the Rhode Island income tax is imposed on the federal taxable income of a resident. RI taxable income is then built only via the RI Schedule M modifications and — new for 2025 — the RI Schedule HR1 add-backs. NEITHER schedule adds back income that is exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty: Schedule M's increasing modifications are the same list as 2024 (out-of-state municipal bond interest, RI fiduciary adjustment, Family Education Account / Tuition Savings Program / Scituate Medical Savings Account recaptures, bonus depreciation, recapture of previously-claimed tax-credit income, pass-through entity tax deducted federally, unemployment compensation not in federal AGI, taxable PPP loan amount), and the new Schedule HR1 add-backs are FOUR BUSINESS DEDUCTIONS ONLY (IRC 163(j) business interest, 174A research and experimental amortization, 179(b) depreciation, 181 sound recording) enacted by P.L. 119-21 — none of them touches treaty-exempt income. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and RI has no add-back of it, it flows through and is not re-taxed by Rhode Island. Therefore RI conforms (treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed).
_strings.@@7cf54629b869: 2025 INSTRUCTIONS FOR FILING RI-1040 (RI Division of Taxation, Revised 11/2025) — Line 4 standard deduction list (Single $10,900; Married Joint $21,800; Qualifying Widow(er) $21,800; Married Separate $10,900; Head of Household $16,350), Line 6 "Exemption Amount: Multiply the number of exemptions in the box by $5,100" with the $254,250 phase-out pointer, Line 7 "Rhode Island Taxable Income: Subtract line 6 from line 5", and Line 8 "Rhode Island Income Tax: Enter the RI income tax from the RI Tax Table or Computation Worksheet". INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED (pass 2) from RI Division of Taxation ADVISORY ADV 2025-22 (November 3, 2025), "Uniform tax rate schedule for Tax Year 2025": over $0 but not over $79,900 pay -- plus 3.75% of the amount over $0; over $79,900 but not over $181,650 pay $2,996.25 plus 4.75% of the amount over $79,900; over $181,650 pay $7,829.38 plus 5.99% of the amount over $181,650 — at https://tax.ri.gov/sites/g/files/xkgbur541/files/2025-11/ADV_2025_22_Inflation_Adjustments.pdf, whose by-tax-year tables also confirm the standard deduction, the $5,100 exemption and the $254,250-$283,250 phase-out range for 2025 specifically. Both passes agree with zero discrepancies.

_strings.@@d6387aa2fd93: Rhode Island Earned Income Credit (RI EITC) — Resident (and part-year/eligible nonresident) taxpayers who qualify for and claim the FEDERAL Earned Income Tax Credit. RI does not impose its own separate eligibility test - if you receive the federal EITC, you receive the RI EITC. You must claim the federal EITC (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 27a) to claim the RI credit.
_strings.@@dfb9d57eb1df: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW RI Schedule HR1 — Individual (first RI add-back schedule aimed at P.L. 119-21, the OBBBA): Rhode Island DECOUPLES from four federal business deductions and adds them back to RI income — the business interest expense deduction (IRC 163(j)), the section 174A research and experimental amortization adjustment, depreciation of business assets (IRC 179(b)), and the qualified sound recording production deduction (IRC 181). None of the four touches treaty-exempt income (see treaty_note). Resolve via: RI Schedule HR1 — Individual and its instructions inside the 2025 RI-1040 instructions booklet (the citation URL); the add-back amounts come from the filer's federal return (Forms 8990/4562 and the 174A/181 deductions actually taken).
_strings.@@e35d3bc27d85: Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Another State — Rhode Island residents who also paid income tax to another state on income that is also taxed by Rhode Island. Authorized under R.I. Gen. Laws section 44-30-18. If credit is claimed for taxes paid to more than one other state, a separate calculation for each state must be made on Form RI-1040MU (page 11 of the RI-1040 Resident booklet); a signed copy of each other-state return must be attached.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: RI-1040, Line 8: "Rhode Island Income Tax: Enter the RI income tax from the RI Tax Table or Computation Worksheet" (Line 7 "Rhode Island Taxable Income. Subtract line 6 from line 5. If zero or less, enter zero"; Line 5 = Line 3 modified federal AGI minus Line 4 RI standard deduction; Line 6 = number of exemptions x $5,100) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2025 Form RI-1040, Line 3 'Modified Federal Adjusted Gross Income' (Line 1 federal AGI from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a, combined with Line 2 net modifications from RI Schedule M; with no modifications Line 3 equals federal AGI). Do NOT subtract anything yourself: the op subtracts the shipped RI standard deduction (Line 4) and the shipped $5,100-per-person exemptions (Line 6) to reach RI TAXABLE INCOME (Line 7), then applies the rate schedule. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — RI-1040 starts from federal AGI (line 1) and taxable_base is Line 3 modified federal AGI (federal AGI +/- RI Schedule M modifications, and for 2025 +/- RI Schedule HR1 add-backs); the op subtracts the standard deduction and the $5,100-per-exemption Line 6 amount. 2025 indexation: the three-bracket structure is unchanged from 2024; the breakpoints rose to $79,900/$181,650 (from $77,450/$176,050), the standard deduction to $10,900/$21,800/$10,900/$16,350 (from $10,550/$21,150/$10,575/$15,850), the exemption to $5,100 (from $4,950), and the phase-out threshold to $254,250 (from $246,450) with the increment rising to $7,250 (from $7,050). The 3.75/4.75/5.99% RATES are unchanged. MFS standard-deduction quirk RESOLVED in 2025: for 2024 the married-filing-separately standard deduction was $25 HIGHER than the single amount ($10,575 vs $10,550) — an artifact of independent rounding. For 2025 both are $10,900. Do not carry the 2024 asymmetry forward. Single rate schedule for every filing status: the 2025 Rhode Island rate schedule is captioned 'FOR ALL FILING STATUS TYPES' (the ADV 2025-22 advisory calls it the "uniform tax rate schedule, which is used by all filers") — the same three brackets (3.75% to $79,900; 4.75% to $181,650; 5.99% above) apply to Single, MFJ, MFS, HoH and Qualifying widow(er); the schedule is duplicated per status here. Qualifying widow(er)/surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly: the RI standard-deduction list gives Qualifying Widow(er) the same $21,800 as Married Joint, so the mapping is exact. Tax-table mandate below $100,000: RI-1040 Line 8 takes the tax from "the RI Tax Table or Computation Worksheet". The table uses $50 bands computed at the band midpoint, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within a table band; the FILED form must use the table below the booklet's threshold. The $100,000 boundary is carried forward from the 2024 pack and was not re-confirmed against the 2025 Tax Table booklet — see `unverified`. Standard-deduction and exemption PHASE-OUT is NOT modeled: if RI-1040 Line 3 (modified federal AGI) exceeds $254,250, BOTH the standard deduction and the $5,100 exemptions phase down in 20-percentage-point steps (factors 0.8000/0.6000/0.4000/0.2000) per $7,250 increment of the excess (rounded UP to a whole increment), and both are $0 once the excess is more than $29,000 (i.e. Line 3 above $283,250 — the range ADV 2025-22 prints as "$254,250 to $283,250"). This op ships the full amounts — taxpayers with Line 3 over $254,250 must use the Standard Deduction Worksheet and Exemption Worksheet on the inside back cover of the 2025 instructions instead. Rhode Island does not allow the use of federal itemized deductions. 2025 RI-1040 instructions, Line 4 reads "Rhode Island does not allow the use of federal itemized deductions" — every filer takes the RI standard deduction shipped here; there is no itemized alternative to model. If someone else can claim you as a dependent on their return, your RI exemption amount is zero (2025 RI-1040 instructions, Line 6 NOTE) — not modeled; such filers should be computed with zero exemptions. NEW FOR 2025 and NOT MODELED — RI Schedule HR1 (Individual): Rhode Island decouples from four federal deductions enacted by P.L. 119-21 (H.R.1, 119th Cong. — the OBBBA) and ADDS THEM BACK to Rhode Island income: the business interest expense deduction (IRC 163(j)), the section 174A amortization adjustment for research and experimental expenditures, depreciation of business assets (IRC 179(b)), and the qualified sound recording production deduction (IRC 181). A filer with any of those federal deductions has a Rhode Island base HIGHER than their federal AGI, and must add the Schedule HR1 amount into the taxable_base supplied to this op. This matters for the same OBBBA-year returns the federal TY2025 pack set covers. taxable_base must be RI-1040 Line 3 (Modified Federal AGI = federal AGI plus/minus net RI Schedule M modifications, plus any RI Schedule HR1 add-backs). Schedule M modifications (out-of-state municipal bond interest add-back, US-government-interest subtraction, the social security modification, and the pension/401(k)/403(b)/annuity modification — which for TY2025 allows up to $50,000 of federally taxable retirement income to be subtracted, with federal-AGI limits of $107,000 single/HoH/MFS and $133,750 MFJ) are NOT computed by this op; with no modifications Line 3 equals federal AGI. Printed-constant rounding in the rate schedule: the second bracket's "Pay" constant is EXACT for 2025 — $79,900 x 3.75% = $2,996.25 to the cent, unlike 2024 where the printed $2,904.38 sat $0.005 above the exact $2,904.375. The third constant still carries the half-cent: printed $7,829.38 vs exact $7,829.375 ($2,996.25 + $101,750 x 4.75% = $2,996.25 + $4,833.125). This pack's brackets use the exact marginal math. Rhode Island's personal and dependent exemptions ARE base reductions (subtracted from income on Line 6 before the rate applies), so they are shipped as exemptions. By contrast, RI's credits — the 16% RI earned income credit (Line 14d, RI Schedule EIC line 41), 25% of the federal child and dependent care credit (RI Schedule I, carried to Line 9a), credit for taxes paid to other states (Line 9b), and the RI-1040H property-tax relief circuit breaker (Line 14c, max $700 for 2025) — are subtracted from TAX, not income, and are NOT applied by this op. No mid-year 2025 rate change: the 3.75/4.75/5.99% structure and the $79,900/$181,650 breakpoints are the final figures, printed in the November 2025 ADV 2025-22 advisory and in the Revised 11/2025 instructions that the 2026 filing season uses.
